# Course data

This page includes information on the provenance of all data used in the course,
as well as instructions on how to download it.

More generally, it is a useful resource on how you can access the thousands of available
extracellular electrophysiology datasets which have been publicshed on open access repositories.
These can be very valuable for testing pipelines, comparing your datasets to others data collected
from the same region or using the same probe, as well as allowing you to do full experiments and analysis.
For example, this recent Paninkki-lab paper was run purely on data access throgh the XXX.

The main open access datasets we will cover come from:
- DANDI archive
- IBL

# Head direction experiment from the DANDI archive
# Used in preprocessing, sorting, postprocessing and Pynapple analysis

The DANDI archive is an open, NIH-backed repository for sharing neurophysiology datasets
in the standardized Neurodata without borders (NWB) file format, which SpikeInterface can load.
You can explore the many datasets on their website, and download them using the Python API (used in this) or Dandi's own command line interface API (here) using the Dandiset ID and the path to the asset you want or DANDI's own API.


The dataset we will use through the majority of this course is hosted on DANDI [here](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41593-024-01588-5). The dataset was used in [CITE]() PAPER. The experiments recorded from the postsubicmum, a brain region XXX, using a 64-channel single channel Cambridge Neurotech probe. They recorded from mice using open-field exploration (as well as during sleep) in
which they measured the head-direction of the mice. They were interested in investigating neural tuning
for head direction (i.e. head-direction tuned neurons fire when the head of an animal is facing a particlar direction or angle).
housands of recordings hosted on DANDI.

The script found [here] can be used to download and store datasets (either the entire recording
or parts of it) using SpikeInterface. For downloading entire dandisets, the DANDI api is also useful.We will use it to download the dataset above, but the same approach works for any of the thousands of recordings hosted on DANDI. Notes on the inner working can be found in comments, the key thing you will need is the asset URL which can be found under the XXX on the file metadata.


# IBL Benchmark dataset
## Used in Preprocessing (part 1)

The [IBL Benchmark dataset](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.26348630) is a curated set of 11
Neuropixels recordings in varied brain regions available publicly via the
[Open Neurophysiology Environment (ONE)](https://int-brain-lab.github.io/ONE/) API.
Data can be streamed directly — no bulk download required.

The script below demonstrates how to:

1. Connect to the public IBL server and select a probe insertion by its `pid`
2. Stream a short snippet of raw AP-band voltage
3. Apply a Butterworth high-pass filter (300 Hz) to remove LFP/DC drift
4. Run the full IBL destriping pipeline (ADC shift correction + spatial k-filter)
5. Open all three stages side-by-side in the `viewephys` interactive viewer

```{.python include="scripts/stream_raw_ephys.py"}
```
